newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products all gain, expect fuel oil.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products all gain, expect fuel oil.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were firmer on Thursday, except for fuel oil, traders said.
Local demand for naphtha remained muted, but prices gained on the back of a stronger NWE .
Full range Skikda cargoes were assessed at $233 cif Med, up $3-4 a tonne.
"The U.S is pulling NWE which is pulling up the Med," said one trader. "The States may be prepared to pay these numbers, but few in Europe will," said another.
Egyptian and Algerian material was pegged around high cif quotes +$2 or so.
Gasoline was about $1 higher around $212 fob for Eurograde material, again on the back of improved NWE prices.

Low sulphur fuel oil settled at lower levels after falling sharply on Wednesday. The market remained long and its recent weakness was confirmed by a deal at around $116 fob NWE. Cif offers into Italy were again pegged at $127.
High sulphur fuel prices were steady to weaker, with new avails of straight-run from the Mideast seen pressuring prices.
Dealers said that two Greek high sulphur straight-run cargoes had been sold in the past couple of days, at around $9 a tonne over the quoted high sulphur high fob.

Gas oil gained around $4 a tonne on stronger futures. Stronger demand supported premiums for Russian 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil at around cif high quotes +$1.50 basis Genoa for mid-month delivery.
A cargo of 33,000 tonnes of Russian was sold at cif high quotes +$1.50 basis Genoa and another of 20,000 tonnes went for cif high quotes +$1 basis Genoa.
Traders saw more bids emerging on Friday and early next week and a continuing dearth of vessels. Demand for other grades of heating oil remained modest.
